sections.h2: Who actually bills property tax in Union County?
sections.html:
Your town does. Union County is made up of 21 municipalities, and the county board's contact page lists a separate tax assessor and tax collector for each one, from Berkeley Heights and Clark to Westfield and Winfield. The county government does not send a bill to homeowners. It runs the Union County Board of Taxation, which supervises assessment and hears appeals.

The Board of Taxation is at 300 North Avenue East in Westfield, open Monday to Friday from 8:00 am to 4:00 pm, at 908-527-4775 or uctaxboard@ucnj.org. For a seller, the split matters: ask your town's collector for a payoff statement and ask your town's assessor about the value on the record.

sections.h2: What does Union County look like on the ground?
sections.html:
Dense, flat and busy with freight and commuters. The county was founded in 1857, covers 105.41 square miles and has Elizabeth as its seat, with 137,298 people in the 2020 count. Only the northwest corner rises above the plain, where the Watchung Mountains reach about 560 feet in Berkeley Heights, and the lowest ground is sea level along the Arthur Kill.

Major roads include the New Jersey Turnpike, the Garden State Parkway, I-78 and I-278, plus routes 1/9, 22 and 24. The Port Newark-Elizabeth Marine Terminal and the southern part of Newark Liberty International Airport lie in Elizabeth. The Census Bureau puts the 2025 population at 601,863 and the land area at 102.77 square miles, or about 5,600 people per square mile in 2020.

A county this tightly packed holds very different housing from one town to the next, from rowhouses in Elizabeth and Plainfield to hillside homes in the Watchung foothills, so the Union County median hides a wide range.

sections.h2: When must a Union County owner file an assessment appeal?
sections.html:
By April 1 in towns that have not revalued, or May 1 in revalued towns, or within 45 days of the bulk mailing of the assessment notice. The Union County Board of Taxation's packet also extends a deadline that lands on a weekend or closed-office holiday to the next business day.

  • Online filers have until 11:59:59 pm on the deadline date, and the system serves copies on the municipal clerk and assessor automatically.
  • Paper appeals must be physically in the Westfield office by 4:00 pm. A postmark does not count.
  • Added, omitted and rollback assessment appeals are due December 1 at 4:00 pm, or 30 days after the collector mails the tax bill.

The county board adds a warning that catches sellers who are behind: taxes and municipal charges must be paid through the first quarter of the current year, or the appeal can be dismissed for failure to pay.

sections.h2: How much does a Union County tax appeal cost?
sections.html:
The filing fee depends on the assessed value of the property, and it is non-refundable. Online filers pay a further $5 convenience charge, and paper filings need exact cash, a check or a money order payable to the Union County Tax Administrator.

Union County tax appeal filing fees by assessed valuation, from the county board's filing packet
Assessed valuationFee
Under $150,000$5
$150,000 up to $500,000$25
$500,000 up to $1,000,000$100
$1,000,000 or more$150

Only an owner or a licensed attorney may file. The board states that real estate agents and appraisers cannot file or sign an appeal for an owner, because the state treats that as unauthorized practice of law. An entity such as a corporation, partnership, LLC or trust must use an attorney unless the prior year's taxes were under $25,000.

sections.h2: How does the Chapter 123 ratio decide whether your assessment is fair?
sections.html:
It sets a value range around your town's average assessment ratio, and you win only if you prove the market value falls outside it. Each year the state studies sales in your municipality and publishes an average ratio plus a lower and an upper limit, spaced 15% below and above the average. You divide your total assessment by each ratio to get a market value range.

If your own estimate of the value on October 1 of the prior year falls inside that range, the board treats the assessment as correct. If you prove a value below the range, the board sets the new value by multiplying the market value by the average ratio. The county notes that the ratios do not apply in a town that has just put a revaluation into effect, because the new assessment is then deemed market value and you only need to prove a figure below it.

sections.h2: What evidence works at a Union County hearing?
sections.html:
Recent arm's-length sales of comparable homes, supplied within the board's timeline. Sales must support the value as of October 1 of the year before the appeal, and the board warns that sales outside the sampling window or between related parties can be disqualified. Sale records are available from your assessor, and you should confirm with the assessor's office that any sale you pick is counted as usable.

  • Evidence not filed with the petition must reach the board at least seven calendar days before the hearing, with copies to the assessor and municipal clerk.
  • Notices go out at least 10 days ahead, and hearings run from April through August, Tuesday through Friday.
  • Hearings take place online or by phone. Adjournments are rarely granted.

The board decides on the evidence submitted, so an explanation of why your comparables fit your house belongs in writing, not saved for a conversation.

sections.h2: What do Union County housing figures show?
sections.html:
Union County is a county of owners and renters in nearly equal numbers, with higher costs than the state's less crowded counties. The Census Bureau's 2020-2024 figures are below.

  • Owner-occupied housing rate: 57.4%.
  • Median value of an owner-occupied home: $529,200.
  • Median monthly owner cost with a mortgage: $3,203, and $1,438 without one.
  • Median gross rent: $1,730.
  • Median household income: $103,202, across 203,277 households.
  • Persons in poverty: 9.7%.

With a median owner payment above $3,200 a month before any repairs, the property tax line is a major piece of what a Union County owner carries, which is why a successful appeal or a clean payoff at closing can change what a seller walks away with.

sections.h2: What if you are selling with property tax owed in Union County?
sections.html:
Contact the collector in the town where the house sits and ask for a written payoff, since every one of the 21 municipalities runs its own office with its own phone line. The county board lists the collector contacts for each town, and the assessor in the same town can tell you whether an added or omitted assessment is pending for new work on the house.

If you think the value is wrong, the appeal cannot be skipped around the sale: the filing windows are fixed, and a new owner steps into whatever appeal is open. Tell the buyer's side about any pending petition so that a hearing notice mailed to the old address does not go unanswered.

faqs.q: Does Union County itself send my tax bill?
faqs.a: No. Each of the 21 municipalities bills its own taxes through its own tax collector. The county supervises assessment through the Board of Taxation in Westfield.

faqs.q: What is the Union County Board of Taxation phone number?
faqs.a: 908-527-4775. The office is at 300 North Avenue East, Westfield, open Monday to Friday from 8:00 am to 4:00 pm, and it can be reached by email at uctaxboard@ucnj.org.

faqs.q: Can my real estate agent file my tax appeal?
faqs.a: No. Only an owner or a licensed attorney may file. The board says agents and appraisers cannot file or sign an appeal for a taxpayer.

faqs.q: Can I appeal if my property taxes are behind?
faqs.a: It can be dismissed. The board requires taxes and municipal charges to be paid up through the first quarter of the current year when an appeal is filed.

faqs.q: When does a Union County tax appeal hearing take place?
faqs.a: Between April and August, Tuesday through Friday, online or by phone. Hearing notices are mailed at least 10 days before the date, and evidence is due seven calendar days beforehand.
